name: Lmc Industries Inc
old_description: Since 1945, we’ve been working with OEMs and tiered suppliers to drive part design innovation that moves businesses forward. In fact, LMC engineering is behind many modern conveniences such as the press-down valve on whipped topping cans!
about:
LMC Industries was founded in 1945 in Arnold, Missouri, by toolmaker Fred Suellentrop, Sr., who set out to build high-quality equipment that would improve the manufacturability of essential products. The company remains family-owned today, operating from a 240,000-square-foot facility in the St. Louis metro area.

The company operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in precision metal stamping — including progressive die stamping, in-die tapping, and in-die assembly — and plastic injection molding, insert molding, and overmolding. It also maintains a 14,000-square-foot tool room equipped with CNC milling, wire and conventional EDM, water jet machining, and TIG welding for in-house die and mold fabrication, repair, and maintenance. Additional in-house capabilities include welding, riveting, chemical passivation, and assembly, supported by partner networks for heat treating and metal finishing.

LMC serves OEMs and tiered suppliers across automotive, agricultural, consumer products, medical device, and hand-tool markets. Its components appear in every major automotive program worldwide, in harvesting equipment and livestock feeding systems, in medical device grips, and in everyday items such as screwdriver handles, toothbrush handles, and the press-down valve on whipped topping cans.

The company differentiates itself by housing both metal and plastic production under one roof, enabling single-source accountability, compressed lead times, and integrated design-for-manufacturability (DFM) reviews across materials. Its quality system follows APQP and PPAP protocols with first-article inspections, and its transfer-tooling process allows it to take over existing programs with minimal disruption.

name: Locust Grove Woodworks
old_description: I have been building fine quality furniture and wood products since 1982. I have had an unusual journey, having been a part of the Amish and related Mennonite groups for most of my life. Their legendary ascetical worldviews had a profound influence on my work and manner of construction.
about:
Locust Grove Woodworks operates from Thorndike, Maine, where the founder has been building fine furniture and wood products since 1982. The owner’s background in Amish and Mennonite communities shaped a philosophy of simplicity, durability, and sustainable craftsmanship that still guides the shop today.

The shop produces handcrafted solid‑wood furniture one piece at a time, using a mix of hand tools, power tools, and draft‑horse‑driven lineshafts. Construction relies on traditional joinery such as sliding dovetails and floating tenons to accommodate wood movement, and finishes are limited to linseed oil and wax. The product range includes beds, chairs, clocks, coffins, cradles, desks, tables, casework, and custom pieces in Shaker, Colonial, and Mission styles.

Customers are primarily residential buyers seeking heirloom‑quality furniture that can be passed down through generations. The maker also serves clients looking for custom casework and specialty items such as coffins and cradles, all built to order without plywood or particle board.

The business was started to create beautiful, enduring furniture in the most sustainable manner possible — originally using only literal horsepower and hand tools. The founder cites the Shaker principle of building as though to live a thousand years but die tomorrow as a guiding ethos, and continues to transition toward horse‑powered generators for electricity.

old_description: Founded in 1994 to exclusively sell factory seconds (cookware that doesn't quite meet our rigorous standards), our Factory Store has since expanded to include the full line of Lodge products. Find everything from our classic
about:
The Lodge Factory Store opened in 1994 in South Pittsburg, Tennessee, as an outlet for factory seconds—cast iron pieces that fell short of the company's exacting standards. Situated next to Lodge's own foundries on the edge of the Cumberland Plateau, the store began as a way to offer discounted cookware directly to visitors and has since grown into a flagship retail location carrying the brand's full product line.

The store stocks the complete range of Lodge cast iron, including classic skillets, Dutch ovens, griddles, and specialty items such as the Fluted Cake Pan and Wedge Pan. Shoppers also find enameled cast iron Dutch ovens, professional-grade carbon steel cookware, stoneware baking dishes, and a wide selection of accessories. The Blacklock collection of lightweight cast iron is featured prominently. Staff provide hands-on guidance on seasoning, cleaning, and recipe ideas, and the store offers custom skillet personalization. Online orders over $75 ship free.

The store serves home cooks, campers, and gift buyers seeking durable American-made cookware. Its customer base includes both walk-in traffic from the Chattanooga area and online shoppers nationwide. The adjacent foundry location allows the store to showcase the manufacturing heritage behind each piece.

The original purpose—to sell factory seconds—remains a draw, but the store now distinguishes itself through direct access to the full Lodge lineup, expert staff, and a setting that connects buyers to the source of the cookware.

name: Loeb Electric
old_description: With four central Ohio electrical supply stores, we proudly serve the local contractor market. Nationally, we partner with the world’s most recognized brands to build, improve, and maintain their stores.
about:
Loeb Electric was founded in 1912 in Columbus, Ohio by Oscar Avery and Arthur Loeb Sr. as the Avery & Loeb Electric Company, initially selling radio and electrical products. After a brief pause during the Great Depression, Arthur Loeb restarted the business under the Loeb Electric name. The company remains family-owned, now led by President Charles Loeb, the third generation of the Loeb family.

Today Loeb Electric operates as one of the largest independent electrical distributors in the United States. From its Columbus headquarters, the company runs four retail stores in central Ohio, four distribution centers totaling over 400,000 square feet of warehouse space, and a fleet of more than 35 delivery trucks. With 350-plus team members, the operation picks over 500 orders comprising 8,000 line items daily. Beyond stocking electrical supplies—lighting, wire, conduit, tools, and EV charging equipment—Loeb provides value-added services including vendor-managed inventory (VMI), project material management, wire cutting and harnessing, supply kitting, and 24/7 locker pickup.

The distributor serves two primary customer groups: local electrical contractors in central Ohio and national brands with multi-site footprints. Its National Accounts division supports retailers and facility operators across the country with preventative and reactive maintenance, energy-saving lighting retrofits, solar and microgrid solutions, and EV charging infrastructure. The company also works with industrial and commercial facilities on energy audits and sustainability programs.

The company emphasizes trust and personal service as its foundation, a philosophy articulated by President Charles Loeb: “This business is about trust. And we’ve earned the trust of our clients, because we provide them with personal service and demonstrate a commitment to their success.” Loeb Electric traces its longevity to continuous investment in experienced associates, technology, and training, aiming to be the partner customers can rely on for on-time delivery and jobsite productivity.

old_description: Lotel was founded in Baton Rouge, Louisiana by John L. about:
Lotel was founded in 1964 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, by John L. Lowery. Shortly after establishing the company, Lowery invented and patented the Mesh-Up line of concrete reinforcement chairs, which became the foundation of the business. The Mesh-Up chair was the first practical flexible chair for welded wire mesh in concrete slabs and gained immediate market recognition.

Today the company operates from its Baton Rouge facility, where it produces Mesh-Up and Rebar-Up chairs for welded wire mesh and rebar support in concrete slabs. The plant runs five injection molding machines and also provides custom molding services for outside clients. Assembly, packaging, and palletized loading are handled in-house.

Lotel’s primary customers are contractors placing concrete slabs, who rely on the chairs for proper reinforcement positioning. The patented chairs have been sold globally, with patent protection in more than 50 countries, including U.S. Patents 6,962,029; 7,458,192; and D491,443.

The company says its chairs were designed for increased stability and ease of use, and that its founding goal was to supply contractors with high-quality products at competitive prices.

name: Louisa Food Products, Inc
old_description: Our mission is to be recognized as the leading provider of high-quality, frozen, filled pasta. To achieve this mission, Louisa Foods stays true to the core values that launched our success from the start.
about:
Louisa Food Products, Inc. operates from St. Louis, Missouri, where it was founded over 50 years ago by Ferdinando Baldetti, a local restaurateur who began producing scratch-made ravioli and pasta for area restaurants. The business remains family-owned, now spanning four generations of the Baldetti family, and continues to be guided by the founding principle that freshness matters.

The company manufactures frozen filled pasta, including ravioli, tortellini, and toasted ravioli, using a scratch-kitchen approach. Each day, vegetables are hand-chopped and roasted, meats are braised and stocks reduced, cheeses are freshly grated, and pasta dough is mixed from semolina flour and eggs. All ingredients are USDA-graded, and production takes place in a facility that includes a culinary center for product development.

Louisa Foods serves both foodservice operators and retail consumers. Its pasta products are supplied to restaurants—often without the diner’s awareness—and are also sold through grocery stores for home preparation. The company markets directly to chefs and home cooks through recipes and pairing suggestions.

The brand differentiates itself by adhering to authentic, labor-intensive methods: no shortcuts, daily from-scratch preparation, and a commitment to fresh ingredients.

old_description: Since 1984, M-TRON Components has maintained a commitment to excellence and has provided our customers with a secure supply chain
about:
M-Tron Components Inc. is based in Ronkonkoma, New York. Founded in 1984, the company is a veteran-owned small business that began as a supplier of electronic components for military and commercial markets.

The company operates as a franchised distributor, stocking a broad inventory of semiconductors, resistors, capacitors, interconnect devices, and computer products from authorized manufacturers. Zager started MADE to give creators a clear, organized path from concept to manufacture, emphasizing collaboration, respect, and inclusivity. MEI Electrical Contractors & Systems Integrators is based in Westfield, Vermont. The company traces its roots to 1991 when it was founded as Mike’s Electric, Inc. in Jay, Vermont. A branch office opened in Williston in 2013 to serve Chittenden County and western Vermont. The fire alarm and security divisions were spun off as MEI Systems Integrators in 2014. In 2017, then‑President Adam Fortier acquired the business and relocated it to a larger facility in Westfield.

Today MEI provides full‑service electrical contracting along with fire alarm and security system design, installation, maintenance, testing, inspection, repair, and monitoring. The firm employs over 65 people, including master and journeyman electricians, certified fire alarm and security technicians, project managers, designers, and estimators. Its capabilities span design/build projects, lighting design and conservation, electrical service upgrades, 24‑hour emergency response, network infrastructure, access control, video surveillance, and fiber optics. Project experience ranges from residential generator installations to multi‑million‑dollar commercial and industrial new construction, including solar and renewable energy work.

MEI serves commercial, industrial, health care, educational, agricultural, governmental (federal, state, and local), and residential customers throughout Vermont and New Hampshire, with government contracts extending into New York, Maine, and Massachusetts. Long‑standing general‑contractor partners include DEW Construction Corp., PeakCM LLC, Bread Loaf Corporation, ReArch Company, Wright & Morrissey Inc., and Kingsbury Companies.

The company emphasizes a “Site Management Strategy” to coordinate schedules, priorities, and participants for turn‑key delivery, and it operates a Customer Alarm Portal for system monitoring. MEI participates in the Vermont Registered Apprenticeship program to train new electricians and highlights its safety record and continuous training. Its stated mission is to provide efficient, quality work on time and on budget while fostering a family‑focused workplace with advancement opportunities.

name: Mace MFG
old_description: In 2023, I took a leap of faith and founded Mace Manufacturing. My tinkering on nights and weekends began with 3D printers and CNC routers. This eventually evolved into acquiring a CNC plasma table to design and fabricate a replacement floor for my 1974 Toyota Land Cruiser. As most of you know, as we get older, our tools just get bigger and more expensive. In February of 2023, I decided to sell my dream car, which was a 1993 Nissan Skyline GTR, to purchase a HAAS VF2 and challenge myself to develop unique and innovative automotive machined accessories.
about:
Mace MFG is based in Indian Land, South Carolina, and was founded in 2023 by Stuart, a mechanical engineer with a background in automotive design and manufacturing. The venture began with nights-and-weekends tinkering using 3D printers and CNC routers, followed by a CNC plasma table to fabricate a replacement floor for a 1974 Toyota Land Cruiser. In February 2023, the founder sold a 1993 Nissan Skyline GT-R to purchase a HAAS VF2 vertical machining center and focus on developing machined automotive accessories.

The company produces precision CNC-machined accessories for off-road Toyota and Lexus vehicles. Its product line includes billet aluminum volume knobs, titanium-and-Ultem key fob cases, polycarbonate-and-Ultem key fob cases, battery tie-downs, shift knobs, drive-mode knobs, front bump stops, rail T-nuts, and battery clamp J-hooks. Manufacturing is centered on the HAAS VF2, supplemented by earlier capabilities in CNC routing, 3D printing, and plasma cutting. Materials used are 6061 aluminum, titanium, Ultem (PEI), and polycarbonate.

Mace MFG serves the automotive aftermarket and overlanding communities, targeting owners of Toyota 4Runner, Tundra, Tacoma, Sequoia, and Lexus GX, LX, and FJ Cruiser models. Sales are direct-to-consumer through the company’s e-commerce site, which offers model-specific fitment. The site also highlights collaborations with other independent makers such as Charvonia Design, Perry Parts, and Teton Workshop.

The business was started to create unique, innovative machined accessories that combine American-made quality with adventurous design. The founder emphasizes engineering-driven development, scrutinizing every detail to deliver rugged gear with reliable performance and no compromise on quality.

about:
Machined In Wood operates from Bellingham, Massachusetts. The shop began as a small, home-based business and has since expanded to serve both individual clients and commercial manufacturers. No founding year or founder names are disclosed in public sources.

The company provides custom CNC woodworking, laser engraving, and finishing services. Its equipment includes two 48" x 48" CNC routers (one with pass-through capability), a horizontal boring machine, CO2 and diode laser engravers, and a 3D printer. Traditional woodworking tools such as a table saw, band saw, jointer, planer, drum sander, and router complement the digital fabrication. They handle production runs from dozens to hundreds of parts and maintain a 1% tolerance level with rigorous quality inspections.

Customers range from hobbyists and local wood shops to engineers and commercial firms requiring prototyping or small-to-medium scale manufacturing. The shop works with wood, plastic, acrylic, and aluminum, and offers painting and finishing including hand painting, airbrushing, HVLP, spar urethane, polyurethane, and nitrocellulose lacquer for musical instruments. They do not produce epoxy river tables or large-scale cabinetry.

Machined In Wood differentiates itself by investing in specialized equipment like the horizontal boring machine and large-format flattening capacity, allowing it to take on smaller, complex jobs that larger shops decline. The team emphasizes nearly two decades of experience collaborating with engineers, proficiency in GD&T, and a policy of not marking up customer-supplied material.

old_description: Mack Molding specializes in custom injection molding, providing high-quality plastic components tailored to diverse industry needs.
about:
Mack Molding was founded in 1920 and is headquartered in Arlington, Vermont, with additional facilities in East Arlington and Cavendish, Vermont, as well as Inman, South Carolina, and Statesville, North Carolina. The company operates as a vertically integrated contract manufacturer across ten locations totaling more than 1.5 million square feet of manufacturing space.

The company provides custom plastic injection molding from 28- to 4,000-ton presses with shot sizes up to 769 ounces, supporting volumes from five pieces to five million annually. Capabilities include large-part molding, structural foam, gas-assist, and two-shot molding, complemented by in-house tooling, CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication (laser cutting, bending, welding), Class A painting, pad printing, ultrasonic welding, and turnkey electromechanical assembly up to Class III medical devices.

Mack serves customers in the medical, industrial, transportation, robotics, energy and utilities, and defense sectors, ranging from Fortune 500 corporations to private enterprises. Its vertically integrated model allows coordination of plastic and metal components from a single location, reducing lead times and ensuring quality across complex programs.

The company emphasizes financial stability — debt-free with a 5A1 Dun & Bradstreet rating — and positions itself as a single partner with total responsibility, leveraging over a century of experience, ITAR and FDA registrations, and certifications including ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016, ISO 14001:2015, and IATF 16949:2016.

old_description: I have been very happy with the three 15kva transformers we purchased from Maddox. The team is ready to please, friendly and actually helpful. The cost vs quality is unfounded. Shipping for these larger units was surprisingly fast too. We will definitely be doing business with them in the future!
about:
Maddox Industrial Transformer was founded in 2015 by a group of transformer industry veterans led by Camden Spiller in Simpsonville, South Carolina. The company is headquartered in Battle Ground, Washington, and operates seven facilities across the United States, including locations in Greer, Pelham, Fountain Inn, and Woodruff, South Carolina; Batavia, Ohio; Moscow, Idaho; and Houston, Texas.

The company designs, manufactures, supplies, and warranties padmount, substation, polemount, and dry-type transformers built to ANSI, NEMA, DOE, and IEEE standards. It also provides pad-mounted and metal-enclosed switchgear. Maddox maintains a large inventory of new and remanufactured units — ranging from 3 kVA mini power centers to 160,000 kVA substation transformers — and offers repair, rewinding, rental, surplus purchase, and parts services nationwide. With over 400 employees, the company has shipped more than 100,000 transformers.

Maddox serves commercial and industrial customers across data centers, manufacturing, renewables, electrical distribution, bitcoin mining, electrical contractors, and real estate development. Its clients range from family-owned businesses to Fortune 100 companies and global data-center hyperscalers. Case studies reference a lumber mill, irrigation district, city electric utility, and solar project.

The company was started to address long lead times and unresponsive service from traditional utility-focused OEMs. Maddox differentiates itself with a "Fast Pass" model for commercial and industrial projects, offering same-day quotes, stock units that can ship in hours, expedited custom production, and direct access to sales engineers rather than call centers.

about:
Majestic Metals was founded in 1979 in Denver, Colorado. For more than 45 years the shop has built a reputation for service, quality, and speed in sheet metal fabrication. Now operating as Majestic Metals by Fathom, the facility continues to serve customers across the Denver region and nationwide from its original location.

The Denver facility provides end-to-end sheet metal fabrication, taking parts from laser cutting and CNC punching through forming, welding, captive hardware installation, finishing, graphics, and final assembly. Equipment includes three fiber and solid-state lasers, two CO2 lasers, five punch presses, thirteen press brakes up to 12 feet and 220 tons, twelve TIG welders, seven MIG welders, and a laser welder. The shop runs lights-out production for quantities of 100 to 10,000 parts and supports projects from prototype through full production.

Core industries include data centers and IT infrastructure, EV charging equipment, medical device housings, self-service kiosks and retail technology, industrial equipment enclosures, military and defense, automotive, energy, agriculture, semiconductor, and consumer electronics and lighting. Customers receive complete fabricated products such as server cabinets, equipment enclosures, control panels, EV charging stations, and analytical equipment.

The company differentiates itself with a single-source model that eliminates multi-vendor friction, a value-engineering approach on every project, design-for-manufacturability support, and a 98% on-time delivery rate. The facility is ISO 9001 certified and ITAR registered, allowing it to handle government and defense work.

name: Manchester Packaging Co
old_description: Founded in 1969, Manchester Packaging Company began business with the goal of providing our customers with quality economical packaging and we continue that tradition today.
about:
Manchester Packaging Company was founded in 1969 in St. James, Missouri, with the goal of providing quality economical packaging. The company remains a custom manufacturer of polyethylene blown film and bags.

The company produces mono-layer and three-layer co-extruded polyethylene film in various slip and clarity grades, including biopolymer blends. It offers flexographic printing from one to eight colors in line or process designs, with both surface and reverse printing options. Finished products include side-seal and bottom-seal bags made to custom sizes, as well as US Postal Service mail overwraps. The facility also recycles 99 percent of its production waste.

Manchester Packaging serves manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, and retail businesses across the packaging sector. Its FDA-approved film is used in applications requiring direct food contact, though specific end markets are not detailed.

The business was started to deliver economical packaging without sacrificing quality, a tradition it says it continues today. Its differentiation rests on in-house extrusion, printing, and converting capabilities that allow custom film and bag constructions within equipment limits.

name: Manufacture Alabama
old_description: is the only trade association in the state dedicated exclusively to the competitive, legislative, regulatory and operational interests and needs of manufacturers and their partner industries and businesses.
about:
Manufacture Alabama operates from Montgomery as the state's sole trade association focused exclusively on the competitive, legislative, regulatory, and operational interests of manufacturers and their partner businesses. The organization represents hundreds of companies ranging from global corporations to small family-owned operations, each described as a vital component of Alabama's economy and job base.

The association provides a suite of services designed to support vibrant manufacturing operations, including environmental, safety, and human resources compliance assistance; government and regulatory representation; workforce development strategies; transportation and infrastructure initiatives; industry promotion; and tax, energy, and other policy support. It also manages member resource groups and industry advisory councils, and operates the Girls Learning About Manufacturing (GLAM) program to encourage female students to pursue manufacturing careers.

Its membership base spans the manufacturing sector broadly, encompassing both manufacturing members and partner members that serve the industry. The association's advocacy and services are directed at the full spectrum of Alabama manufacturers, from large international firms to small local shops.

name: Maple Lane Farms LLC
old_description: A 5-generation family farm with a colorful and wholesome history. Our story is one of determination and never giving up. Farming has never been easy, and so to keep up the good fight we’ve diversified. We offer hay, feed sales, and custom processing for your beef & pork. We now have a retail store as well as currently selling locally raised beef, pork, and chicken. You order in a call-in manner, we fill it for you and call you when it’s ready. To our current customers, thank you for choosing us, and to our new visitors, welcome, and we hope to become friends soon. As always, cash, check, credit, debit, and EBT are accepted.
about:
Maple Lane Farms operates from Charleston, Maine, on a property first purchased by Stanley Higgins in 1935. The farm passed to Charles “Shine” and Margaret Higgins in 1941, became Charles C Higgins & Son in the 1960s, and was renamed Maple Lane Farms in 1999 when Barry and Mary Higgins bought the operation. It remains a fifth‑generation family‑owned business run by the Higgins family.

The farm raises naturally grown beef — typically maintaining around 700 head — along with pork, chicken, and lamb. A state‑inspected processing facility, expanded in 2005 and again in 2011 to add refrigeration and an automated smoke house, handles custom slaughter and cutting for customers’ own animals as well as the farm’s own stock. Products are hand‑cut, sealed, and flash‑frozen with no aged inventory. The farm also produces and sells horse‑quality round and square hay bales (stored indoors and net‑wrapped), silage by the ton, and screened compost made from processing, cow, and horse waste.

Customers include local households purchasing retail cuts through the on‑farm store (open Monday–Friday with call‑in ordering), farmers needing custom processing for their livestock, horse owners seeking hay, and gardeners using the compost. The business historically served wholesale channels but now focuses on direct‑to‑consumer and custom‑processing sales.

The Higgins family diversified into meat processing, hay, and compost to keep the farm viable amid changing regulations and market pressures. They emphasize that every step — from cutting to labeling — is done by hand, not by high‑speed automation, and that products go straight from the cutting room to the freezer to ensure freshness.

name: Mar-Med
old_description: Physician founded, family owned, since 1989 Medical device manufacturer and global distributor
about:
Mar-Med was founded in 1989 in Grand Rapids, Michigan, by Dr. Joseph Marogil, a general surgeon who invented the Tourni-Cot digital tourniquet to address a need he encountered in hand surgery cases. The company remains physician-founded and family-owned.

Today Mar-Med operates as an FDA-registered medical device manufacturing site certified to ISO 13485:2016. It designs and distributes a line of disposable devices including the Tourni-Cot and Uni-Cot digit tourniquets, the Rhino-Pak epistaxis balloon, the Balloon Extractor for nasal foreign-body removal, the Derma-Stent abscess and cyst drain, and the ZEROWET wound irrigation system. The company serves emergency medicine, podiatry, pediatrics, orthopedic surgery, and other specialties, shipping to healthcare facilities worldwide.

Mar-Med's customer base spans hospital emergency departments, surgical centers, and clinics across the U.S. and internationally. Its products are used in procedures ranging from digit laceration repair to epistaxis control and nasal foreign-body extraction.

The company states its mission is to create growth and opportunity in its community through the manufacture and distribution of effective medical devices that support efficient procedures, positive patient outcomes, and a healthy bottom line. Mar-Med also emphasizes sustainability, composting label backing paper, recycling eligible waste, and reusing cardboard and scrap paper.

Marelli North America, Inc. is headquartered in Lewisburg, Tennessee. The company operates as part of the global Marelli group, whose motorsport division has developed electronic and electro-mechanical systems for two- and four-wheel racing vehicles since 1919. No founding year or ownership details for the North American entity are disclosed in the available sources.

The company designs and manufactures electronic and electro-mechanical systems for motorsport applications, including telemetry, hybrid and electric powertrain systems, and fuel components. Beyond racing, its portfolio spans automotive lighting, electronics, interiors, propulsion, exhaust, chassis, thermal management, and software-defined vehicle platforms. Marelli reports 32 global sites certified under SA8000 and describes itself as a $10 billion startup, though specific facility size and headcount for the Lewisburg location are not provided.

Marelli serves automakers and racing teams across series such as Formula 1, MotoGP, and the World Endurance Championship. Its customer base includes carmakers seeking technology transfer from motorsport to passenger vehicles, as well as partners in the software-defined vehicle ecosystem. The company emphasizes co-creation with customers, suppliers, and technology partners from early development stages.

Marelli positions its motorsport operation as an accelerator for technology development, leveraging an agile, fast, and optimized design model to flow innovations from track to road. The company highlights its co-creation engagement model, sustainability commitments—including 88% renewable electricity use and 100% of innovation projects aligned with Design for Sustainability criteria—and a culture where employees act as owners of the business.

about:
Marina Foods, Inc. was established in 1964 as a family-owned and operated business in a modest warehouse in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. The company relocated to a new facility in Medley, Florida (western Miami) in 2007, positioning itself centrally in South Florida's tri-county area between the Port of Miami and Port Everglades.

The company manufactures and packs a range of edible oils — including soybean, corn, canola, peanut, sunflower, and olive — as well as shortenings (liquid and solid), vinegars, cooking wines, mayonnaise, salad dressings, and sauces. It offers private labeling, custom formulations, and multiple packaging options spanning retail, food-service, and bulk shipments. A fleet of tractor-trailers supports fast delivery across Florida and the United States, while bilingual customer-service representatives coordinate domestic and international shipping logistics. The firm also provides commodity-market insight tied to the Chicago Board of Trade.

Marina Foods serves food-service companies throughout North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean, as well as Italian food distributors seeking olive oils, blends, and specialty dressings such as creamy Italian, Caesar, blue cheese, and ranch. Products are sold under the Marina brand and two house brands, Chef's Recipe and DiMarco, in both retail and food-service sizes.

The company emphasizes quality assurance, with processes monitored, measured, and reviewed as required by law. It cites competitive pricing, quick order and delivery times, and ongoing recipe development as keys to its reputation in the southeastern United States and global markets.

The company's resource library supplies technical data sheets and specifications for each product family.

Marine Tech emphasizes domestic production, stating that all cables are manufactured at its York, Pennsylvania facility. The firm was recently recognized as the 22nd fastest-growing company in the Central Pennsylvania region, reflecting its expansion in the specialty cable market.

about:
Marlin Steel was founded in 1968 in Baltimore, Maryland, initially producing bagel baskets. The company is led by Drew Greenblatt, who has overseen its expansion from a single Baltimore facility to additional locations in Indiana and Michigan, nearly tripling in size over the past four years.

The company manufactures custom-engineered products from steel wire and sheet metal, including material handling baskets, wire forms, and mobile carts. Its capabilities encompass wire forming (0.003" to 0.625" diameter), sheet metal fabrication (0.03" to 3" thick), steel machining and fixturing, welding, and more than 40 coating finishes such as electropolishing, Teflon, Nylon, Halar, powder coating, and plastic coating. Robotic stamping, coining, swaging, and piercing machines support automated production.

Marlin Steel serves aerospace, defense, medical, food processing, automotive, data center, and telecommunications industries. Examples include sanitary stainless steel carts and baskets for medical and pharmaceutical use, telecom equipment enclosures and wire management solutions, automotive wire baskets that improve production tolerances, aerospace engine floats and turbine fan blade carriers, and electropolished baskets for food processing compliance.

The company differentiates itself through its "Quality Engineered Quick®" approach, leveraging advanced automation and precision engineering to deliver rapid turnaround. Greenblatt emphasizes a community-focused culture that invests in employees with wages and growth opportunities, aiming to strengthen the rural communities where its facilities operate.

name: Marsh Electronics, Inc.
old_description: Discover Marsh Electronics: 90 Years of Innovation in Electronics Distribution
about:
Marsh Electronics traces its roots to 1935 when Earl Marsh and Kathleen Meek opened Marsh Radio Supply Co. at a storefront on West State Street in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The business rebranded as Marsh Electronics in 1973 and, after a period of acquisitions by Sterling and Marshall, returned to independent ownership in 1998. Today the company operates from its headquarters in Milwaukee, serving the North Central United States from a 20,000-square-foot facility in West Allis.

The firm functions as a broad-line distributor of electronic and electromechanical components — capacitors, circuit breakers, connectors, sensors, switches, and more — while also running a value-added division, MarVac Assemblies, that produces custom cable assemblies, wire harnesses, and other built-to-print products. In-house capabilities include Komax wire-cutting and stripping equipment, custom assembly workstations, and an engineering team that supports component selection, circuit design, and qualification testing. Additional services encompass inventory replenishment programs and vendor-reduction solutions.

Marsh serves original equipment manufacturers and tier‑2/3 suppliers in commercial and off‑road vehicles, energy (including solar heliostat tracking and energy‑storage systems), food and beverage processing, general industrial, medical devices, and military applications. The company highlights UL‑ and CSA‑compliant assemblies for off‑road vehicle wiring and provides Country‑of‑Origin and Proposition 65 labeling as required.

Differentiators cited by the company include over 90 years of industry experience, ISO 9001:2015 certification, a dedicated engineering and technical sales staff, and a focus on custom solutions tailored to OEM needs rather than simply maximizing sales volume.

about:
Marsh Medical operates from Newell, West Virginia, as a dedicated medical component brand under Marsh Bellofram, a U.S. manufacturer with a history exceeding 125 years. The division was created to consolidate nearly five decades of experience supplying critical components to the medical device industry.

The company designs and manufactures pressure and flow regulators, electro-pneumatic controls, transducers, electronic timing controls, and open medical power supplies. In-house engineers and chemists develop custom solutions, drawing on a portfolio of more than 100,000 custom parts that include precision air regulators, diaphragms, silicone components, and electrical wiring. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Marsh Medical added a second production shift running six days a week to meet surging demand for ventilator components.

Customers are primarily medical device original equipment manufacturers, including ventilator makers and other critical care equipment suppliers. The brand positions itself as a single access point for streamlined procurement of medical device components.

Marsh Medical emphasizes convenience, faster service, and streamlined procurement, leveraging its pandemic-era mobilization and the deep manufacturing heritage of Marsh Bellofram to offer a more effective way to source medical parts.

old_description: Meidensha Corporation has been providing employees with hands-on safety education designed to stimulate danger sensitivity since 2008. In December 2016, Meidensha Corporation also began selling on-site education for clients seeking it at plants, construction sites and other locations outside the Company. Hands-on safety education is more effective than other methods, and is helping eradicate workplace accidents. Lessons that simulate the experience of workplace accidents are provided in all-weather hands-on safety education vehicles that eliminate the need for student movement.
about:
Meiden America Switchgear, Inc. is headquartered in Gray Court, South Carolina, near Greenville. The company was founded in 2020 as a subsidiary of Meidensha Corporation, a Tokyo-based manufacturer established in 1897. President Yukihiro Takeshita leads the operation, which celebrated its grand opening and first shipment on February 9, 2021.

The facility designs, manufactures, tests, and sells high-voltage vacuum circuit breakers (VCBs) at 72.5 kV and 145 kV ratings, along with vacuum interrupters (VIs). Its dead-tank VCBs use dry air as the insulating medium, eliminating the need for SF6 greenhouse gas. The parent company has produced vacuum interrupter bottles since 1967 and introduced the world's first 72.5 kV dry-air insulated VCB in 2002; more than 2,500 of those units have been delivered worldwide, including over 1,000 to North American customers. A 145 kV dry-air VCB followed in late 2021.

Primary customers are North American electric power utilities and original equipment manufacturers that integrate VIs into their own switchgear. The company serves the power and energy sector and also lists automotive testing systems among its industries.

Meiden America states its mission is to lead the industry by providing high-value products that integrate cutting-edge technology drawn from 125 years of experience. The focus is on helping utilities and OEMs transition away from SF6 dependence toward environmentally conscious solutions.

about:
Methode Electronics was founded in 1946 by William J. McGinley on the south side of Chicago, Illinois. The company’s name originated from an anagram combining “good manufacturing method” with “electrode and cathode of a vacuum tube.” McGinley, a World War II veteran, established the business on the principle that innovation and cutting‑edge technology could engineer solutions to help customers grow. The corporate headquarters later relocated to Southfield, Michigan, where the company operates as a global supplier of custom‑engineered mechatronic products.

Methode designs, engineers, and manufactures user‑interface systems, LED lighting, power‑distribution assemblies, and sensor solutions for original‑equipment manufacturers. Its vertically integrated production spans assembly, decorating, electronics, metalworking, plastic molding, and testing across global design, engineering, and manufacturing centers in North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. The company employs approximately 6,500 people and operates dedicated production lines, clean‑room facilities, and prototype prove‑out cells to support programs from prototype through high‑volume serial production.

The company serves transportation markets including automotive, commercial vehicle, e‑bike, aerospace, bus, and rail; cloud‑computing infrastructure; construction equipment; consumer appliances; military and aerospace; renewable energy; data‑center and storage; industrial equipment; energy storage; robotics; and power conversion. Its branded divisions—Methode Electronics Automotive Group, Grakon, Nordic Lights, Power Solutions Group, Hetronic, TouchSensor, and Methode Sensor Technologies—address specialized segments such as mining, material handling, agriculture, forestry, marine, locomotive, drone, medical‑device, vending, and fitness‑equipment OEMs.

Methode emphasizes proprietary and differentiated technology, deep cross‑application expertise, highly vertically integrated manufacturing, quality and reliability, and responsiveness to global OEM needs as its core differentiators. A disciplined product‑development system with validation testing underpins its ability to deliver custom‑engineered solutions at scale.

Metro Plastics Technologies LLC, founded in 1975, operates from Noblesville, Indiana. The company began as a plastic injection molding business and has grown into a custom molder with a newly constructed, custom-built facility in the Midwest.

Metro manages 650 unique active molds, some with up to 12 cavities cycling every 22 seconds, producing between 35 and 50 million parts annually. Value-added services include in-mold labeling, custom automation, custom packaging, and engineering support for material selection, mold analysis, and manufacturability.

Testimonials reference clients such as Moonlight Concepts LLC, O2 Blast, and AM Leonard, indicating work in consumer, industrial, and specialty markets. The company also offers domestic and offshore tooling sourcing and participates in the MAPP Association plastics community.

Metro emphasizes relationship-driven service, backing its commitment with an on-time delivery guarantee that offers a 10% discount if a shipping date is missed. about:
MiDAS Foods International operates from its main campus in Oak Park, Michigan, with a second facility in Birmingham, Alabama. The company has been developing dry blends for commercial kitchens for over 40 years. Leadership includes partners Richard Elias, serving as president, and Gary Freeman, executive vice president of corporate development.

The company manufactures custom dry blends for sauces, seasonings, glazes, gravies, soups, batters, and dessert mixes. Its combined R&D and manufacturing footprint exceeds 150,000 square feet across the two U.S. sites, supplemented by an affiliate plant in Kashipur, India, that ships to more than 20 countries. The culinary team, led by executive chefs Jerry McDonald and Casey Schallert, handles formula development, clean-label systems, and plant-based ingredient platforms.

MiDAS supplies casual dining restaurant chains and food processors nationwide. Restaurant customers use the blends to replace scratch-made sauces and reduce prep time, while manufacturers incorporate them as single-ingredient solutions to cut SKU count, storage costs, and shipping weight. Regional product lines cover North/Midwest flavors such as Michigan baked bean seasoning and beer cheese fondue, and South/Southeast items like Alabama white barbecue sauce and Nashville hot sauce mix.

The company emphasizes that its dry blends lower total cost by minimizing shipping, eliminating refrigeration, and cutting waste. It also promotes custom formulation capabilities that match or exceed scratch culinary standards while improving batch consistency and production throughput.

about:
Micro Metals, Inc. was founded in 1972 by Kenny Driscoll in Colorado Springs, Colorado, at an elevation of 6,272 feet. The company remains family-owned and operated by the Driscoll family, who have grown it into a single-source manufacturer of precision metal parts serving customers across the Midwest, West, and South from its Rocky Mountain location.

The 141,000-square-foot facility, backed by 208,000 square feet of secured outside storage, houses three automated laser cutting systems, a high-capacity robotic press brake, robotic and manual welding cells, CNC machining centers (VMC, HMC, VTC), coil punching and rollforming lines, and an automated powder- and liquid-coating division certified for CARC paint. An experienced workforce—machinists average 15 years on the shop floor and the engineering team includes military veterans—supports in-house design, engineering, assembly, and finishing.

Micro Metals serves the telecommunications, U.S. military, energy, climate-control, construction, and secure-storage sectors, supplying local, national, and international clients. The company also produces components for humanitarian building projects on four continents, including orphanages in Venezuela, rehabilitation centers in Eastern Europe, a food-distribution center in Haiti, and a medical center in Africa.

The Driscoll family started the business to provide a one-stop partner that can quote, design, fabricate, assemble, and ship under one roof, eliminating the need to outsource finishing or assembly. Automated processes and ISO 9001, NADCAP, and CARC certifications enable consistent quality at scale, while the Colorado Springs location offers transportation efficiencies for rapid delivery.

about:
Micro-Precision Technologies, Inc. (MPT) was founded in 1998 in Salem, New Hampshire. The company focuses on thick-film hybrid microelectronics and semiconductor packaging designed for harsh environments.

MPT produces thick-film circuits screened onto ceramic substrates such as alumina, aluminum nitride, and beryllium oxide, offering a robust alternative to traditional FR-4 printed circuit boards. Its capabilities include FR-4 to ceramic substrate conversion, hybrid assembly with both manual and automated surface-mount technology, wire bonding (ball and wedge), die attach with automated dispensing for epoxy, encapsulant, or optical fluid, and semiconductor die repackaging for improved thermal performance or pinout configuration. All assembly work is performed in a Class 10,000 cleanroom, and the company supports new product introduction as well as consigned or full turnkey assembly.

The company serves industrial, military, and medical markets. Its products are used in applications that demand operation under extreme heat, high vibration, downhole mining conditions, deep-sea wells, and space environments, including power semiconductor packaging challenges.

MPT emphasizes the inherent thermal management of ceramic substrates, which dissipate heat more efficiently than epoxy-based FR-4, and maintains certifications including MIL-PRF-38534 Class H qualification since 1998, QML-38534 listing, DSCC certification, AS9100D, ISO 9001:2015, and ITAR registration.

about:
MicroLink Devices was founded in 2000 in Niles, Illinois, a northern suburb of Chicago. The company operates a 30,000-square-foot facility that includes a clean room and device fabrication and test laboratory.

The company designs and manufactures III-V epitaxial materials for wireless devices and high-efficiency, single- and multi-junction GaAs-based solar cells and sheets. Its proprietary epitaxial lift-off (ELO) process removes the solar cell structure from the growth substrate, yielding lightweight, flexible cells while allowing substrate reuse. MicroLink owns metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) tools for high-volume epitaxial growth, along with full fabrication and test capabilities for semiconductor devices and solar cells. It also performs contract research and development, having served as a prime federal contractor on more than thirty programs since 2003.

MicroLink's products serve the aerospace, defense, and renewable energy sectors. Its solar cells and sheets are used in unmanned aerial vehicles, spacecraft, and terrestrial solar collectors. The epitaxial materials support cellular phone and wireless device manufacturers. The company has been a prime contractor on over thirty federal programs developing solar cells, transistors, and lasers.

The company emphasizes quality control, with ISO 9001 certification and a policy of verifying customer specifications before production. Its technical staff includes recognized experts in GaAs and InP device growth and processing, supporting customers through development and production. The ELO technology, developed through federal R&D programs, differentiates its solar products by enabling lightweight, flexible cells with reduced cost through substrate reuse.

Mid America Steel Inc is based in Fargo, North Dakota. Founded in 1905 as an agricultural repair shop and foundry, the company has evolved into a modern steel fabrication firm. It is employee-owned, a structure the company says supports its workforce dedication and community involvement.

The company provides custom metal fabrication including structural steel, pressure vessels, tanks, rebar, plate steel, and miscellaneous metals such as aluminum and stainless steel. Mid America Steel serves a broad range of industries across North America. Its fabricated steel products have been used in industrial plants, wastewater treatment facilities, sports arenas, government buildings, hospitals, commercial buildings, agricultural facilities, oil and gas structures, schools, churches, and flood control projects.

The company emphasizes strong customer relationships, willingness to tackle complex projects and tight deadlines, and attributes its capabilities to its skilled, employee-owned workforce. It holds certifications from ASME, AISC, AWS, and the Canadian Welding Board, and operates as an ASME stamp holder for pressure vessels and an AISC-certified fabricator with in-house AWS and CWB certified inspectors.

about:
Milco Industries, a family-owned textile manufacturer, has operated from Bloomsburg, Pennsylvania since its founding in 1922. Now in its second century, the company is led by President and CFO Sabrina Hunsinger, with Travis Carr heading sales and Justin Wark serving as general manager. The business began as a warp knit fabric producer and has remained in the same central Pennsylvania location for over 100 years.

The company runs a fully vertical operation at its Bloomsburg facility, handling knitting, dyeing, and finishing under one roof. Its forming capabilities cover tricot, raschel, and circular knitting, complemented by pad dyeing, brushing, unbroken-loop (UBL) finishing, calendering, and a range of specialty finishes such as anti-microbial, UV-resistant, fire-retardant, and moisture-management treatments. The plant also offers color matching, fabric analysis, direct-to-fabric and heat-transfer printing, and in-house quality control with lab testing on every production batch.

Milco serves a broad spectrum of markets with products that include netting, mesh, suede, satin, jersey, stretch spandex, hook-compatible loop fabrics, and print substrates. Customers can source custom-developed fabrics, commission dyeing and finishing services, or draw from a stock program. The company's ANSI-compliant and performance-oriented textiles find use in applications requiring durability, safety, and specific functional properties.

Milco emphasizes its Made-in-USA production, ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system, and a shipping process designed to exceed customer requirements. The firm's longevity and vertical integration allow it to control quality from yarn to finished fabric, a differentiator it highlights alongside its commitment to veteran employment.

The firm differentiates itself through its nearshore Tecate operation—one hour from San Diego—and its early creation of an e-commerce PCB assembly service (Screaming Circuits) for rapid prototyping. A recent poll cited 96% customer confidence in its handling of material constraints.

StaySure® was developed in collaboration with gastroenterologists and targets a condition more prevalent than asthma.

Minnesota Medical Technologies serves the global medical device market, focusing on patients, physicians, and healthcare providers managing fecal incontinence. The company sells directly and through clinical channels worldwide.

The founders started the company because they believed existing fecal incontinence products were inadequate—failing to prevent leakage, control odor, or provide ease of use. Their mission is to deliver continence care products of unmatched performance, comfort, and quality, grounded in a genuine understanding of the daily challenges patients face.

about:
Mitas Electronics is based in Round Rock, Texas, and has accumulated over 17 years of operating history. The company was founded as an engineering-led organization focused on miniature high-speed interconnect systems, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and manufactures miniature high-speed cable assemblies and interconnect systems, providing interconnect engineering, manufacturing coordination, and technical support. Its capabilities span application review, mechanical fit, signal-path awareness, DFMA, supply chain management, process documentation, and quality-focused execution across manufacturing partners. Mitas also produces technical binders—engineering resources that include connector specifications, application guides, and manufacturability considerations for cable assembly designers. To date, the company reports shipping more than 4 million cables, serving over 500 customers, and delivering more than 2,200 tailored solutions.

Mitas serves customers in high-speed data transport, electronic systems, and computing infrastructure markets. Its technical binders and interactive viewers support established interconnect families such as QSFP-DD, CABLINE-CA II, and CABLINE-VS II, catering to engineers who need dimensional context, inspection guidance, and application-specific selection support.

about:
Mitchell Furniture Systems traces its roots to Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where William Mitchell founded the company in 1896 to produce dairy farming equipment such as automatic stalls and stanchions. The business expanded into steel products for parks and playgrounds before pivoting in the 1940s to folding leg tables, choral risers, and wall-mounted table and bench systems for cafeterias. Today the company operates manufacturing plants in Fredonia and Milwaukee, maintaining a “Made in America” commitment with seasoned metal fabricators and assemblers using both time-honored techniques and robotic welding.

The product line centers on wall-mounted table and bench systems (NPX and ST series), mobile tables with integrated seating (PorTables), fold-and-roll tables (Fold-N-Roll), convertible 3-in-1 ConverTables, adjustable-height folding tables (Saturna and Fold-O-Leg), and risers for stages and seating. Production combines steel frame fabrication, robotic welding, wood top machining, and final assembly. The company also offers a table-top replacement service for both its own and competitors’ tables.

Primary customers include K–12 school districts, universities, municipalities, churches, corporate offices, and conference centers. Historical markets encompassed dairy farming and municipal park systems. The company cites installations in cafeterias, fellowship halls, classrooms, lecture halls, and theaters as typical applications.

Mitchell emphasizes that its products are engineered for decades of service, noting that many risers sold in the late 1940s remain in use. The firm differentiates itself through domestic manufacturing, robotic welding for consistency, and a willingness to retrofit competitors’ tables with Mitchell tops.

name: Monterey Mills
old_description: Sliver knitting, or high-pile knitting, is a process that locks individual fibers into a lightweight knit backing. The length of acrylic fibers used adds dimension and warmth to the fabric, when needed, without adding additional weight. Other advantages of using acrylic fibers include the incorporation of colorfast dyes and, a finished fabric that is odor and mildew resistant. The end result is a light, soft, comfortable fabric that is warmer than fleece and is machine washable and dryable.
about:
Monterey Mills operates from Janesville, Wisconsin. The company traces its current ownership to February 1995, when Dan Sinykin purchased the former Roller Fabrics after a seven-month unpaid trial period. Sinykin, a Drake University graduate, had previously built a 14-store retail tailor chain and spent six years in sales and marketing at Procter & Gamble. He consolidated multiple manufacturing facilities and expanded the business into automotive, equestrian, apparel, hospital, and pet-product markets.

The mill specializes in sliver knitting (also called high-pile knitting), a labor-intensive process that locks individual acrylic fibers into a lightweight knit backing to create fabrics that are warmer than fleece yet machine washable. An in-house research and development team controls fiber and yarn selection, pile height, density, tensile strength, width, color, and stitch count, enabling custom performance fabrics for diverse applications. The company produces rolled fabrics, paint-roller fabrics, and finished goods for medical, pet, blanket, and bedding lines, all marketed as Made in USA.

Customers span medical and pet-product manufacturers, blanket and bedding brands, automotive and equestrian suppliers, apparel makers, and hospital procurement. The technical team works directly with clients to develop fabrics that meet specific performance requirements, from odor and mildew resistance to colorfastness.

Monterey Mills positions itself as one of the few remaining practitioners of sliver knitting, a craft many competitors abandoned due to its complexity. The company emphasizes sustainability, sourcing recycled raw materials, repurposing all production waste, and treating and reusing wastewater. Continuous improvement in processes and employee skills is cited as the foundation for its quality reputation.

Montrose Molders operates from Piscataway, New Jersey, where it was founded in 1966 by William Bruce Wilson. The firm runs a vertically integrated operation that covers part design, tooling, molding, extrusion, assembly, and packaging. Its molding department comprises 51 presses ranging from 40 to 1,000 tons of clamp force, supported by two extrusion lines with co-extrusion capability. An on-site tool room builds aluminum and steel production molds, while a 25,000-square-foot assembly area can run five lines simultaneously. Mold-flow simulation uses SolidWorks Plastics software, and industrial design services help translate concepts into 3D models.

Montrose serves customers in retail, battery, automotive, lighting, safety, aerospace, electronics, medical devices, and consumer goods. The company positions itself as a contract plastics manufacturer for original equipment manufacturers and brand owners seeking a single-source partner from prototype through full-scale production.

Management emphasizes a one-stop-shop model intended to shorten lead times, reduce costs, and deliver consistent quality. Each program is assigned a dedicated project manager, and engineering resources span industrial design to tooling validation. The family legacy is cited as a driver of long-term customer relationships and continuous investment in equipment and process control.

It emphasizes optimizing product design through deep knowledge of material and process selection, and providing fast, consistent service from development proposal through to sales.

about:
Moulstown Woodworks operates from a log yard in the Pigeon Hills of York County, just east of Abbottstown, Pennsylvania. The business is run by Wade, who offers a mobile sawmilling service under the motto “can mill, will travel.” No founding year or ownership structure is disclosed on the company’s website.

The core service is on-site portable sawmilling using a 2021 Woodmizer LT40, a fully hydraulic commercial mill with a 34-inch cutting width and capacity for logs up to 20 feet long. Typical output runs 250–300 board feet per hour, with milling priced at $75 per hour plus a transportation and setup fee starting at $85 for sites within 10 miles of the yard. The company also provides yield estimates and pre‑job site visits.

Customers include landowners, arborists, excavators, forestry consultants, lumber buyers, kiln operators, furniture makers, carpenters, and luthiers across south‑central Pennsylvania (Adams, Cumberland, Perry, Lancaster, Chester, and York counties) and northern Maryland (Frederick, Carroll, Baltimore, and Hartford counties). Repeat clients are noted in towns such as Gettysburg, Hanover, New Oxford, and Westminster.

The business emphasizes customer preparation—clean, metal‑free logs staged for the mill, adequate labor to clear slabs, and equipment to move heavy logs—as the key to efficient yield. The mobile model eliminates the need for customers to transport logs to a fixed mill.

Its prefabricated piping assemblies, launchers and receivers, and valve settings are used to reduce field construction costs for customers in those markets.

name: Nashville Electric Service - Music City Solar
old_description: The city spoke. We listened. Thanks to the voice of our customers, what once was a landfill off I-65 is now the site of Nashville's first community solar park that includes 17,020 panels, available to participating customers, marking an important step in offering clean, efficient, maintenance-free energy.
about:
Music City Solar is a community solar program operated by Nashville Electric Service (NES), a publicly owned utility headquartered in Madison, Tennessee. The program was launched on August 1, 2018, when the utility transformed a former landfill off Interstate 65 into Nashville’s first community solar park. NES developed the project in direct response to customer demand for renewable energy options.

The solar park comprises 17,020 photovoltaic panels and feeds clean electricity directly into the NES grid. Residential and commercial customers can subscribe to individual panels and receive a monthly bill credit for the energy produced through 2038. As of the latest data, 3,142 panels have been leased, generating over 21 million kilowatt-hours, while 12,863 panels remain available for subscription. The utility also administers the Solar Angel Fund, which accepts tax-deductible donations to provide energy assistance for low-income households; 1,015 panels have been donated to that effort.

The program serves NES’s residential and small-business customers across the Nashville metro area, including renters who cannot install rooftop systems. It also partners with The Community Foundation of Middle Tennessee to distribute Solar Angel funds locally. Pinnacle Financial Partners is noted as a financial collaborator.

NES frames the initiative as a way to align the utility’s offerings with the city’s rapid growth and environmental goals. By locating the array on a reclaimed landfill and requiring no maintenance from subscribers, the program aims to make solar participation accessible and maintenance-free while fostering community engagement through shared energy credits and charitable giving.

old_description: Nebraska Prep Equipment was founded by Cory Hart and Jamison Wallman in late 2017. While building their last catering kitchen for their then 5-year-old catering business, they were faced with the task of sourcing quality used equipment to stay within budget. Cory and Jamison found that quality used equipment was few and far between locally, so they broadened their search area and found a great amount of quality used equipment in the larger cities throughout the Midwest. Instead of keeping this treasure hidden, Jamison and Cory decided to start transporting this equipment back to Southeast Nebraska, cleaning the equipment and reselling it at a fair price to other food service companies in the area. Nebraska Prep Equipment started to gain traction and the option for new equipment was added to our inventory eventually leading to the offering of new equipment with manufacturer warranty as well as occasional new scratch and dent units at a discounted price.

Nebraska Prep Equipment is based in Adams, Nebraska. The company was founded in late 2017 by Cory Hart and Jamison Wallman. The pair had operated a catering business for five years and, while building a new kitchen, struggled to find quality used equipment locally. They began traveling to larger Midwestern cities to source reliable used pieces, transporting them back to southeast Nebraska, cleaning them, and reselling them to other food‑service operators in the area.

Today the business operates as a food‑service equipment dealer with a showroom on South 82nd Road in Adams. It sells both refurbished used equipment and new units backed by manufacturer warranties, along with occasional scratch‑and‑dent items at reduced prices. The showroom is open by appointment only, and the company emphasizes personal service throughout the buying process.

The customer base consists of locally owned restaurants, caterers, and hospitality businesses throughout the region. The founders’ original catering peers were among the first buyers, and the company continues to focus on independent food‑service operators rather than large chains.

Hart and Wallman started the venture because quality used equipment was scarce in their area. They differentiate themselves by combining a curated selection of used and new brands with what they describe as unparalleled customer service during and after the sale.

The company emphasizes start-to-finish project collaboration and value-added engineering support.

The founders and subsequent owners built the business on predictable outcomes and supply-chain reliability. Leadership states that the goal is to be a low-risk partner that delivers parts on time and within budget, backed by scientific process control and a culture of continuous improvement.

Nimbletronics serves engineers and OEMs across semiconductor, medical, telecommunications, defense, security, audio, video, industrial, energy, radio-frequency, and network markets. Customers typically require rapid iteration on complex designs, such as fine-pitch BGAs, chip-scale packages, stacked die, and rigid-flex circuits.

North Dakota Soybean Processors (NDSP) operates a soybean crushing facility in Casselton, North Dakota. The company was formed as a joint venture between CGB Enterprises, Inc., a private U.S. grain and transportation company with a 50-year history, and Minnesota Soybean Processors (MnSP), a cooperative processor. The partnership was established to create a local, year-round market for soybeans grown in Cass County and the surrounding Red River Valley, adding value to the region’s harvest and stimulating the local economy.

NDSP processes soybeans into three primary products: food-grade soybean oil, soybean meal for livestock feed, and soyhull pellets. The plant is described as a state-of-the-art facility designed to serve both food and fuel markets, with the oil directed toward food users and the renewable diesel sector, while the meal supports the livestock industry. The company also offers producers a blended portfolio of pricing tools and contract options to manage market risk.

The facility serves soybean growers across North Dakota and western Minnesota, providing a reliable outlet for their crops. Its customer base includes food manufacturers, renewable fuel producers, and livestock operations that require consistent, high-quality meal and oil. By processing locally, NDSP reduces transportation costs for farmers and supplies domestic end-users with a traceable, North Dakota-origin product.

The venture was driven by a mission to sustainably produce and deliver high-quality soybean products while fostering a safe, supportive environment for employees and the community. Leaders from both parent organizations emphasized the plant’s role in creating jobs, generating tax revenue, and strengthening the agricultural economy of the region.

OMG Tooling Inc. was founded in 1980 by Oliver Marino Gerardi in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Gerardi began by leasing a small space and operating a tool and die shop, sketching initial concepts on napkins before translating them into tooling and molds. The company expanded in 1992 when Gerardi purchased land and constructed its first dedicated building, establishing a foundation for full-service injection molding.

The company provides end-to-end plastic injection molding services, encompassing custom product design, in-house tooling fabrication, and molding production. OMG maintains internal tooling capabilities—including advanced tool building, tooling enhancements, and transfer tooling management—that many competitors have outsourced. Its engineering team automates molding processes to achieve consistent quality at competitive production rates, positioning the firm as a domestic alternative to overseas sourcing.

OMG serves original equipment manufacturers across a diverse set of sectors: consumer goods, healthcare, sports and leisure, construction, transportation, infrastructure, electronics, technology, and industrial markets. Customers frequently transfer existing molds to OMG for continued production, leveraging the shop’s expertise in tooling preservation and part quality improvement.

The company emphasizes its strategic location in central Oklahoma, which offers supply-chain advantages for U.S. distribution, and its commitment to 'Made in USA' manufacturing. Founder Oliver Gerardi’s original values—integrity, excellence, quality, dedication, loyalty, and customer service—remain the stated guiding principles for the business.

old_description: The best pressure filter company depends on the specific filtration requirements, industrial application, and performance needs. Oberlin Filter is a leading provider of high-quality filtration solutions that effectively remove up to 99.99% of suspended solids from liquids.
about:
Oberlin Filter Company is based in Pewaukee, Wisconsin. The company has over 60 years of proven experience in filtration technology, though a specific founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures pressure filtration systems that remove up to 99.99% of suspended solids from liquids down to 1 micron. Its core process uses 40 PSI of pressure to force contaminated fluid through filter media, automatically discharging captured contaminants as a dry cake rather than wet sludge. Product lines include the OLIMIN8R™ for single CNC machine coolant filtration and the Hot Oil Filter for large-scale food processing, along with systems for metal finishing, sulfur recovery, maritime scrubbers, breweries, chemical processing, semiconductor wastewater, crystallizer zero-liquid-discharge, and industrial wastewater. The company reports serving more than 380 manufacturers, from Fortune 500 firms to local machine shops.

Oberlin’s filters are used across industrial coolants, metal finishing, food processing oil, sulfur recovery, maritime scrubbers, breweries and sluice dewatering, chemical processing, semiconductor and solar wastewater, crystallizer ZLD applications, and industrial process wastewater. Customers range from global Fortune 500 manufacturers to small job shops.

The company emphasizes that its differentiation lies in the automatic dry-cake discharge, which eliminates wet sludge disposal issues, reduces filter media costs by up to 80%, and delivers a typical return on investment within 6 to 12 months. The 40 PSI pressure system is described as four times more powerful than gravity-based filtration.

about:
Ogonek Custom Hardwoods operates a sawmill in Barberton, Ohio, serving the Northeast Ohio region. The business grew from a family’s connection to the area, with Dan Ogonek the operation. While the exact founding year is not publicly stated, the company describes its origin as growing out of a family’s love for a place that represents more than an investment.

The sawmill specializes in custom cutting beams and timbers for timber-frame construction and home-improvement projects, including decorative beams and mantels. It can produce lengths up to 52 feet in species native to Northeast Ohio such as white pine, red oak, aspen, white oak, cherry, and black walnut. Offerings include rough-cut, non-kiln-dried material, tongue-and-groove milling, specialty blocking and dunnage, planing and ripping dimensional lumber, live-edge milling, hand-hewn beams, and installation of decorative beams.

Customers range from timber-frame builders and owner-builders to contractors renovating historic homes. Testimonials cite a cabin rebuild in Illinois and Wisconsin using 6×10 pine timbers 20 feet long, a hand-built timber-frame pavilion with planed white pine and tongue-and-groove decking, and decorative beam installation in an 1800s farmhouse. The company also supplies rough-sawn, planed, and live-edge material for various custom woodworking projects.

Ogonek emphasizes sustainably sourced local lumber and hands-on expertise; Dan Ogonek is noted for providing timber-framing suggestions drawn from experience. The crew’s focus on pride in workmanship, from wood selection to joinery, is highlighted in customer feedback as a distinguishing trait.

about:
Oklahoma Shirt Company operates from Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, where it was founded by a team passionate about design, craftsmanship, and Oklahoma culture. The shop began as a screen printing and apparel business focused on creating custom products that celebrate the people, businesses, and communities of the state.

The company provides custom screen printing, embroidery, direct-to-film (DTF) printing, signage, stickers, graphic design, promotional products, and online gear stores. Screen printing requires a minimum of 24 garments per design, while DTF and embroidery start at five items. Standard production turnaround is one to two weeks after artwork approval and payment, with rush service available for a 50 percent upcharge.

Clients include businesses, schools, organizations, and event planners across Oklahoma, as well as retail customers purchasing Oklahoma-, OSU-, and OU-branded merchandise. The company serves as the official printing partner of the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Oklahoma Shirt Company emphasizes thoughtful design, quality materials, and modern production to deliver products that build connection and tell a story. An in-house design team handles everything from quick shirt layouts to full SIM process separations and branding packages.
